name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
instructions: Set the shoulder pads so you can stand tall with a slight knee bend, then place the balls of your feet on the platform edge with your heels hanging free.
Stand up to load the pads onto your shoulders, brace your core, and keep your legs nearly straight.
Lower your heels slowly below the platform until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Drive through the balls of your feet to rise as high as possible onto your toes.
Pause and squeeze at the top, then lower under control into the next rep.
formCues: Keep knees nearly straight to bias the gastrocnemius
Use a full range: deep stretch at the bottom, full contraction at the top
Control the descent and avoid bouncing
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom using the tendon rather than the muscle
Cutting the range of motion short at the top or bottom
Bending the knees to heave the weight up

name: Seated Calf Raise (Machine)
instructions: Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform with your knees bent about 90 degrees under the pads.
Adjust the thigh pads snugly over your lower thighs and release the safety lever.
Lower your heels toward the floor until you feel a strong stretch in your calves.
Press up through the balls of your feet, lifting your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze briefly at the top, then lower slowly and under control.
formCues: Bent knees shift emphasis to the soleus
Move only at the ankles and keep the thighs still
Pause at peak contraction on every rep
commonMistakes: Using momentum or bouncing through reps
Cutting the range short at the bottom
Loading too heavy and shortening the stretch

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place the balls of your feet low on the platform with heels hanging off the edge and legs nearly straight but knees unlocked.
Release the safety handles and support the weight on the balls of your feet.
Let your toes flex back slowly, lowering the platform until you feel a deep calf stretch.
Extend your ankles to push the platform away, pressing through the balls of your feet.
Pause at full extension, then lower under control into the next rep.
formCues: Keep knees nearly straight, never locked, throughout
Press through the balls of the feet, not the whole foot
Keep a controlled tempo with no rapid bouncing
commonMistakes: Locking the knees and straining the joint
Letting the platform drop fast and out of control
Placing the feet too high so the heels cannot drop for a stretch

name: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or weight plate, holding a dumbbell in one or both hands at your sides.
Stand tall with legs straight, core braced, and heels hanging off the edge.
Lower your heels toward the floor until you feel a full stretch in your calves.
Drive up onto the balls of your feet, raising your heels as high as you can.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly into the next rep.
formCues: Keep legs straight to target the gastrocnemius
Use a step or plate for a fuller stretch at the bottom
Lightly touch a wall for balance if needed
commonMistakes: Bouncing instead of controlling each rep
Using a short range of motion at the top and bottom
Rolling the ankles outward instead of pressing straight up

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on one foot with the ball of that foot on a step or raised surface and the heel hanging free.
Hold a wall or rail lightly for balance and hook the non-working foot behind your working ankle.
Lower your heel below the step until you feel a deep stretch in the calf.
Press up onto the ball of your foot, lifting your heel as high as possible.
Pause at the top, lower under control, and finish all reps before switching legs.
formCues: Use the rail only for balance, not to assist the lift
Keep the working knee straight but not locked
Aim for a full stretch and full contraction each rep
commonMistakes: Pulling on the rail to help raise the body
Rushing reps and losing the stretch
Letting the ankle roll inward or outward

name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Place the balls of your feet on the platform of a donkey calf raise machine with heels hanging off, hinge at the hips to about 90 degrees, and settle the pad across your hips or lower back.
Hold the front support, keep your legs nearly straight, and brace your core.
Lower your heels toward the floor until you feel a deep stretch in your calves.
Press up through the balls of your feet, raising your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly and under control.
formCues: Hinge at the hips to load the gastrocnemius under stretch
Keep knees nearly straight throughout
Emphasize a slow, controlled stretch at the bottom
commonMistakes: Bending the knees to push the weight
Bouncing out of the bottom position
Rounding the lower back instead of hinging at the hips

name: Smith Machine Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Set a weight plate or sturdy block under the bar and stand with the balls of your feet on it, heels hanging off.
Position the Smith machine bar across your upper traps and unrack it by rotating the hooks free.
Stand tall with legs nearly straight, then lower your heels until you feel a full calf stretch.
Press up through the balls of your feet, lifting your heels as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze at the top, then lower under control into the next rep.
formCues: Use a plate or block under the toes for a full range of motion
Rest the bar on the traps, not the neck
Drive straight up without bending the knees
commonMistakes: Skipping the toe block and losing the stretch
Bending the knees to assist the lift
Bouncing at the bottom instead of controlling the stretch
